intro: Here in Konya province, a god still lies in the quarry where he was cut. The Fasıllar Monument dates from the 13th century BC: a seven-metre unfinished Hittite statue showing the storm god standing on the shoulders of a mountain god.
history: The seven-metre statue was never finished, and it lies where it was cut, in its own quarry. It shows the storm god standing on the shoulders of a mountain god, with lions at either side. It is thought to have been carved for the sacred pool at nearby Eflatunpınar, yet it was never moved.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the unfinished statue, the quarry, the lion figures and the tool marks.
facts: Did you know? This is the largest Hittite statue known in Anatolia, and at some seventy tonnes it was never lifted at all. The seven-metre figure lies where it was cut, in its own quarry, and was never finished.
outro: This brings our journey through the Fasıllar Monument to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
